title: Northgate Protect Coverage Terms, Start Events and Waiting Periods
content:
Each Northgate Protect tier has a coverage term in calendar months, an event that starts coverage, and a waiting period: the calendar days after coverage starts during which no claim is accepted when the plan was bought after the item had already been fulfilled. A waiting period of 0 days means there is none.

| Tier | Coverage term | Event that starts coverage | Waiting period after coverage starts (plan bought after fulfilment) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Northgate Protect Standard 2-Year | 24 calendar months | The covered item's fulfilment date | 0 days (none) |
| Northgate Protect Standard 3-Year | 36 calendar months | The covered item's fulfilment date | 0 days (none) |
| Northgate Protect Accident 2-Year | 24 calendar months | The covered item's fulfilment date | 30 days |
| Northgate Protect Accident 3-Year | 36 calendar months | The covered item's fulfilment date | 30 days |
| Northgate Protect Accident 4-Year | 48 calendar months | The covered item's fulfilment date | 30 days |
| Northgate Protect Complete Monthly | 1 calendar month, renewing monthly | The enrollment date | 30 days |

## Notes on the table

- The single-item tiers start coverage on the date the covered item was fulfilled; Northgate Protect Complete Monthly starts on the date the customer enrolled.
- The waiting period applies only where the plan was bought after the item had been fulfilled. A plan bought before or on the fulfilment of its item carries no waiting period on any tier.
- *Hypothetical:* an Accident 3-Year plan bought after its item was fulfilled has a 30-day waiting period after coverage starts; the same plan bought at the register together with the item has none. A Standard tier never has one, because its waiting period is 0 days.
